What the searches did surface about Colbun's investment communications: disclosures are framed around CapEx guidance and project pipeline, not explicit return thresholds. 2025 total CapEx ~US$500m (~US$430m growth / ~US$70m maintenance); 2026 items include BESS Chaca (~US$50m), BESS Diego de Almagro Sur (~US$130m), Don Eduardo Substation (~US$24m). On profitability logic, management stated that BESS projects are always linked to a PPA and the company does not rely on the difference of prices for that project's profitability — a qualitative strategy statement, NOT a numeric hurdle rate. Growth pipeline: Junquillos wind (473 MW, Chile), Bayovar wind (660 MW) and Algarrobal PV (400 MW) in Peru; plus stated intent to enter Spain via a first acquisition then greenfield build-out. None of these carry a stated target IRR or WACC.

Non-official / third-party figures (NOT company hurdle rates, therefore not recorded as disclosures): a simplywall.st analyst narrative cited a discount rate of ~12.13% (down from ~12.31%) used in their own valuation; a University of Chile student valuation thesis used a WACC in a DCF; research literature notes green bonds cut WACC ~25bps generically. Colbun's first international green bond (US$600m, 3.15% coupon, 2032) finances renewables — a financing cost, not an investment hurdle. All of these are external/analyst-derived, not a return threshold the company states it uses for investment decisions.

Recommendation: to confirm definitively, the primary sources most likely to address this (and that I was blocked from reading) are the Memoria Integrada 2024 (colbun.cl/docs/.../2504_colbun_memoria2024_v9_.pdf) and the Q2/Q3/Q4 2025 earnings-call transcripts and presentation decks on colbun.cl/corporativo/inversionistas.
